label: Site analytics
what: Visitors, users and sessions for the last 7 days, the top pages and the top sources, from Google Analytics 4.

credentials.label: Service account key file
credentials.help: The path to the JSON key file on this computer. Only the path is stored. The file is read by the feed and never shown.

credentials.label: GA4 property id
credentials.help: The numeric id of the property. In Google Analytics open Admin, then Property settings (or Property details). It is not the G- Measurement ID.

reads: Page views, users and sessions for 7 days against the 7 before.
The top 8 pages by views and the top 3 traffic sources.
not_reads: Anything outside the one property you add the account to.
scopes: Viewer on your Google Analytics property, for the service account only.
steps: In Google Cloud turn on the Google Analytics Data API for a project.
Create a service account and download its key as a JSON file. Keep the file outside the Quarterdeck folder.
In Google Analytics open Admin, then Property access management, and add the service account's email as a Viewer.
Enter the path to the key file here and save it.
Enter your numeric property id in the GA4 property id field here and save it. Admin, then Property settings, shows it. It is plain digits, not the G- Measurement ID.

Optional: to make each item link to your site, set ga4.site_url (for example https://example.com) in {data_folder}/config/integrations.json. A ga4.property_id set in that same file works too, and the field here wins when both are set.
Switch Site analytics on. The openssl command is needed. It is already on a Mac and on most Linux systems.
revoke: In Google Analytics remove the service account from Property access management. Delete the key in Google Cloud, then remove the path here.
tested: Parsing tested against sample data only; not tested against the real service.
